news.title: All White Matt Garbett turns World Cup heartbreak into a lesson in resilience
news.lede: All White Matt Garbett entered uncharted territory when an innocuous training incident in June stymied a boyhood dream and put a roadblock in his professional football career. This year's Football World Cup was meant to be a turning point for Garbett and a showcase of his talents. Instead a hamstring injury suffered two days before New Zealand's opening game of the global tournament led to instant disappointment, months of turmoil and a journey of self-discovery. Days before returning to the field for the All Whites in a home series against India this week, Garbett can look back and see the positives.

news.title: NFF Honors Flamingos for Historic U-17 Women's World Cup Triumph
news.lede: The Federation said the triumph had brought pride to the country and further strengthened Nigeria’s position on the global football stage. The NFF Acting General Secretary, Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, and members of the federation’s management made the commendation on Monday during a visit to the victorious players at their hotel in Abuja. Ikpeme, who conveyed the appreciation of the NFF and the entire Nigerian football family, commended the players for their hard work, discipline and dedication, urging them to remain focused on achieving greater success.He said the Federal Government and Nigerians were proud of the team, adding that their achievement had placed the country in the history books as the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. He also noted that Nigeria had become the first African country to win both the male and female editions of the FIFA U-17 World Cup.“.

news.title: Ben White reveals heartbreaking reaction to missing World Cup and response to England boos
news.lede: Ben White revealed missing the last World Cup left him in tears. The Arsenal defender, 29, is famed for quitting the England camp in Qatar in 2022. But White’s reaction to missing out last summer through injury paints a very different picture of a player who insists it is still his dream to play for his country in a major tournament. White was exiled from the England set-up for four years until Thomas Tuchel brought him back in March, only for injury to ruin his chances of going to the United States.

news.title: The Young boy who took a football to bed and woke up a World Cup player
news.lede: Mitchell Prest playing for the Young Cherrypickers as a junior and during his time with the North Queensland Cowboys. Photos: Gay Prest and 13 Bati/Facebook. As a boy growing up in Young, Mitchell Prest rarely went anywhere without a football tucked under his arm. He carried it around the house, took it with him when his parents sent him to do jobs and, according to his mother Gay, even slept with it like a pillow.
